answer: Each agent can submit work only after its public key is bonded to a scarce, nontransferable credential issued through in-person verification, and the protocol caps how much influence any credential receives. A violet-colored credential is no stronger than a marble one; changing keys or spinning up copies does not multiply voting weight. To forge identities, an attacker must recruit and verify more real people, paying for coordination and risking that those participants revoke credentials or expose the operation.
